title: Etale splitting of an integral fibre with normal residue fields
statement:
Let $A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $D$ is integral over $A$ (every element satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$). Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset D$ be primes with inverse image $\mathfrak p$. Assume that there are finitely many primes of $D$ over $\mathfrak p$ and that for every such prime $\mathfrak r$, the extension $\kappa(\mathfrak r)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is algebraic and normal and has finite automorphism group over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; here $\kappa(\mathfrak r)=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak r)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, and normal means that all minimal polynomials split. There exist an etale $A$-algebra $B$ (meaning $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]), a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset B$ over $\mathfrak p$, a prime $\mathfrak q'\subset D'=B\otimes_A D$ contracting to both $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$, and an isomorphism of $B$-algebras
$$D'\simeq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n,\qquad n\geq1,$$
such that each $D_j$ is integral over $B$ and has exactly one prime $\mathfrak q_j$ over $\mathfrak p'$, each $\kappa(\mathfrak q_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is purely inseparable, and $\mathfrak q'$ is the prime of $D'$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q_1$. Purely inseparable means that in positive characteristic every element has some $p$-power in the base field, and in characteristic zero the extension is trivial. Tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with their usual algebra multiplication. No finite-dimensionality of the full residue extensions and no finite-generation assumption on $D$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, applied when residue extensions are normal with finite automorphism groups, as explicitly done in pione.tex, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, second reduction paragraph. Finiteness of their maximal separable subextensions follows from fields.tex Tag 0BR4 (lemma-normal-embeddings-differ-by-aut), Tag 09HJ (lemma-separable-degree), and Tag 030K (lemma-separable-first); the chosen prime is lifted through the nonzero tensor product of the two residue fields.

proof.text: Enumerate the finitely many primes $\mathfrak r_i$ of $D$ over $\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-dl-a1-normal-finite-aut-separable-subfield] to each normal algebraic extension $E_i=\kappa(\mathfrak r_i)$ of $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: its separable subfield $F_i$ is finite-dimensional. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $F_i/k$ is separable and $E_i/F_i$ is purely inseparable. This uses no finiteness of the full fields $E_i/k$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, hypothesis (2), and pione.tex Tag 0BST, second reduction paragraph; field-theoretic justification by fields.tex Tags 0BME, 0BR4, 09HJ, 030K

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-integral-finite-residue-model] to these separable subfields. Obtain a finite A-subalgebra C of D, with D integral over C, bijective contraction on the primes over p, and intermediate residue subfields L equal to the ranges of the residue maps from C; each E/L is purely inseparable. The finite-model result also records finiteness of L over the base residue field.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, construction of the finite intermediate algebra

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure Omega of kappa(q), obtaining a geometric point t_q of D and its restriction phi to A. Restriction from geometric points of D to those of C is bijective: surjectivity follows from integral lying-over and the existence of geometric points; injectivity follows from the fibre-prime bijection and the fact that two field embeddings agreeing on L agree on its purely inseparable extension E. For the latter, residue-field maps agree on the model by their universal property, and then use injectivity of restriction along a purely inseparable field extension.

proof.text: Apply the geometric-point etale idempotent theorem to the finite algebra C and phi. Transport its complete orthogonal idempotents to B tensor D. Tensor-product points over phi_B correspond exactly to the original points over phi; the restriction bijection shows that each transported idempotent selects exactly one point. Enumerate the finite set so that the point extending the prescribed q has index zero. It is nonempty because t_q exists.

proof.text: Set D_j=(B tensor D)/(1-e_j). Complete orthogonal idempotents give an isomorphism with the finite product of these quotients (Mathlib CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.bijective_pi). Integrality persists under tensor base change and quotients. The selected point descends to each quotient. Every point on the quotient takes e_j to one, so it is that selected point. Every prime over ker phi_B has a geometric point by integral geometric-point existence; therefore the fibre prime is unique. The unique-point residue criterion gives the canonical purely inseparable residue map. Kernels commute with ring-map composition, yielding all contraction formulas and the specified prime in factor zero.
